patterns.name: eval() with User-Controlled Input
patterns.description: eval() called with data from req, body, params, query — direct RCE vector.

patterns.name: Function Constructor Code Injection
patterns.description: new Function() with dynamic string — equivalent to eval(), executes arbitrary JS.

patterns.name: Shell Exec with Template Literal Injection
patterns.description: exec/execSync called with a template literal containing user variables — OS command injection.

patterns.name: child_process with User-Controlled Input
patterns.description: child_process methods called with req/query/body data — unambiguous RCE.

patterns.name: Node vm Module with User Input
patterns.description: vm.runInNewContext with user data — sandbox escape leads to RCE.

patterns.name: Python exec()/eval() with User Input
patterns.description: exec() or eval() called with user-supplied data in Python — direct RCE.

patterns.name: Python subprocess with shell=True
patterns.description: subprocess with shell=True — command injection if any part is user-controlled.

patterns.name: os.system() with Dynamic Input
patterns.description: os.system() with f-string or concatenation — OS command injection.

patterns.name: SQL Injection via Template Literal
patterns.description: SQL query built with template literal embedding user variables — parameterize all queries.

patterns.name: SQL Injection via String Concatenation
patterns.description: Raw SQL built with + operator and a variable — use parameterized queries.

patterns.name: SQL Injection via Python Format String
patterns.description: Python %s / .format() used inside SQL query string.

patterns.name: NoSQL Injection via Unvalidated Request Data
patterns.description: MongoDB find/findOne receiving unvalidated req data — NoSQL injection.

patterns.name: LDAP Injection Risk
patterns.description: LDAP query constructed with user input — can bypass authentication.

patterns.name: XPath Injection Risk
patterns.description: XPath expression built with user-controlled data — authentication bypass possible.

patterns.name: Log Injection with User Input
patterns.description: Logging user-controlled input directly — attacker can forge log entries.

patterns.name: HTTP Response Header Injection
patterns.description: User input placed directly into a response header — header splitting attacks.

patterns.name: Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI)
patterns.description: Template engine render called with user-controlled template string — SSTI leads to RCE.

patterns.name: Dynamic RegExp from User Input (ReDoS)
patterns.description: new RegExp() with user input — can trigger catastrophic backtracking to hang server.

patterns.name: Hardcoded Password in Source
patterns.description: Password literal assigned directly in code — use environment variables.

patterns.name: Hardcoded JWT Secret
patterns.description: JWT secret is a literal string — tokens can be forged offline.

patterns.name: JWT Algorithm: none Accepted
patterns.description: JWT verification allows algorithm:none — tokens accepted without signature.

patterns.name: JWT Decoded Without Signature Verification
patterns.description: jwt.decode() instead of jwt.verify() — signature is never checked.

patterns.name: bcrypt with Insufficient Salt Rounds
patterns.description: bcrypt saltRounds below 10 — hashes are cheap to crack.

patterns.name: Plain-Text Password Comparison
patterns.description: Password compared with === instead of bcrypt.compare — implies plaintext storage.

patterns.name: MD5/SHA1 Used for Password Hashing
patterns.description: MD5/SHA1 are broken for password hashing — use bcrypt, scrypt, or argon2.

patterns.name: Hardcoded Express Session Secret
patterns.description: Session secret is a literal string — sessions can be forged.

patterns.name: Auth Cookie Without HttpOnly Flag
patterns.description: Session/auth cookie without httpOnly — accessible from JavaScript.

patterns.name: Auth Cookie Without Secure Flag
patterns.description: Auth cookie without Secure flag — sent over HTTP.

patterns.name: User Role / isAdmin Read from Request Body
patterns.description: Privilege controlled by client-supplied field — mass assignment attack.

patterns.name: Token Compared Without Timing-Safe Method
patterns.description: === comparison on HMAC/tokens is vulnerable to timing attacks — use crypto.timingSafeEqual.

patterns.name: Math.random() for Security Token
patterns.description: Math.random() is not cryptographically secure — use crypto.randomBytes() or crypto.randomUUID().

patterns.name: Broken Cipher Algorithm
patterns.description: DES/3DES/RC4 are cryptographically broken — use AES-256-GCM.

patterns.name: AES-ECB Mode Used
patterns.description: ECB mode leaks plaintext patterns — use AES-GCM or AES-CBC with random IV.

patterns.name: Hardcoded Initialization Vector
patterns.description: Static IV defeats CBC/CTR mode security — generate a fresh IV each time.

patterns.name: Hardcoded Encryption Key
patterns.description: Encryption key embedded as a string literal — any encrypted data can be decrypted.

patterns.name: SSL/TLS Certificate Verification Disabled
patterns.description: Certificate verification disabled — all HTTPS connections are MITM-able.

patterns.name: TrustAllCerts Disabled in Java/Android
patterns.description: Custom TrustManager accepts all certificates — all TLS is MITM-able.

patterns.name: Python random Module for Security Values
patterns.description: random.randint/choice used for tokens — use the secrets module.

patterns.name: AWS Access Key ID
patterns.description: AWS Access Key ID hardcoded in source.

patterns.name: AWS Secret Access Key
patterns.description: AWS Secret Access Key in source — gives full API access.

patterns.name: GitHub Personal Access Token
patterns.description: GitHub PAT detected.

patterns.name: Slack API Token
patterns.description: Slack bot or user token detected.

patterns.name: Stripe Secret Key
patterns.description: Stripe sk_live_ or sk_test_ key detected.

patterns.name: Google API Key
patterns.description: Google API key — may allow billing fraud.

patterns.name: SendGrid API Key
patterns.description: SendGrid API key detected.

patterns.name: Private Key PEM Block
patterns.description: RSA/EC/OpenSSH private key embedded in source.

patterns.name: Database Connection String with Credentials
patterns.description: Database URL with username:password — use environment variables.

patterns.name: Generic Secret / API Key Hardcoded
patterns.description: Secret variable assigned a string literal — store in environment variables.

patterns.name: Discord Bot Token
patterns.description: Discord bot token — full control over the bot account.

patterns.name: NextAuth Secret Hardcoded
patterns.description: NEXTAUTH_SECRET as literal string — session tokens can be forged.

patterns.description: innerHTML assigned a variable — XSS sink if user-controlled.

patterns.name: Open Redirect via location Assignment
patterns.description: window.location set from URL params — open redirect or DOM-based XSS.

patterns.name: Auth Token in localStorage

patterns.name: href with javascript: Protocol
patterns.description: javascript: URI in href executes script.

patterns.name: dangerouslySetInnerHTML in React
patterns.description: dangerouslySetInnerHTML bypasses React XSS protections — only safe with DOMPurify-sanitized content.

patterns.name: CORS Wildcard with Credentials
patterns.description: Origin:* with credentials — enables CSRF from any origin.

patterns.name: Path Traversal via readFile with User Input
patterns.description: fs.readFile with user-controlled path — attacker can read arbitrary files.

patterns.name: Arbitrary File Write with User Input
patterns.description: fs.writeFile with user-controlled filename — can overwrite any file.

patterns.name: path.join with Unvalidated User Input
patterns.description: path.join alone does NOT prevent traversal — use path.resolve + prefix validation.

patterns.name: Multer Upload Without fileFilter
patterns.description: multer() without fileFilter — any file type including web shells can be uploaded.

patterns.name: Python open() with User-Controlled Path
patterns.description: open() called with request data — reads/writes arbitrary files.

patterns.name: Python pickle.loads()

patterns.name: Python yaml.load() Without SafeLoader
patterns.description: yaml.load() without SafeLoader deserializes arbitrary Python objects.

patterns.name: Java ObjectInputStream Deserialization
patterns.description: Java native deserialization — RCE via gadget chains.

patterns.name: Java XMLDecoder Deserialization
patterns.description: XMLDecoder can execute arbitrary Java — never use with untrusted input.

patterns.name: fetch() with User-Controlled URL

patterns.name: Node http.get with User URL
patterns.description: Native HTTP client with user-controlled URL — SSRF.

patterns.name: Open Redirect via res.redirect
patterns.description: res.redirect() with user-controlled URL — open redirect and SSRF.

patterns.name: Python requests with User-Controlled URL
patterns.description: requests called with URL from user input — SSRF.

patterns.name: Java DocumentBuilderFactory Without XXE Protection
patterns.description: DocumentBuilderFactory without disabling external entities — XXE reads arbitrary files.

patterns.name: Java SAXParser Without Secure Processing
patterns.description: SAXParserFactory without secure processing — XXE injection.

patterns.name: Python xml.etree Without defusedxml
patterns.description: Parsing XML with stdlib xml.etree — use defusedxml instead.

patterns.name: Direct __proto__ Assignment
patterns.description: Assigning to __proto__ pollutes Object.prototype.

patterns.name: constructor.prototype Assignment
patterns.description: Modifying constructor.prototype from user keys pollutes the prototype chain.

patterns.name: Object.assign with User Input
patterns.description: Object.assign merging user-controlled object — prototype pollution via __proto__ key.

patterns.name: lodash _.merge with User Input
patterns.description: Recursive merge with user input — prototype pollution via __proto__ key.

patterns.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_ on Secret Variable
patterns.description: NEXT_PUBLIC_ variables are bundled into the client — never use for secrets.

patterns.name: Next.js API Route Without Auth Guard
patterns.description: API route handler with no session/token check — may be publicly accessible.

patterns.name: Next.js Server Action Without Auth
patterns.description: Server Action writing to DB without auth check — any client can trigger it.

patterns.name: React href with User-Controlled Value
patterns.description: href from user data — javascript: URIs lead to XSS.

patterns.name: Next.js cookies().set() Without Security Options
patterns.description: Auth cookie without httpOnly/secure — exposed to JS and HTTP.

patterns.name: Request Body Reflected in Response
patterns.description: res.send/json with req.body directly — reflected XSS or data leak.

patterns.name: Error Stack Trace Sent to Client
patterns.description: Sending error.stack to client — leaks file paths and library versions.

patterns.name: CORS Reflecting Request Origin
patterns.description: Reflecting incoming Origin header without a whitelist — any origin gets CORS access.

patterns.name: Dynamic require() with User Input
patterns.description: require() with user input path — loads arbitrary modules.

patterns.name: express.json() Without Size Limit
patterns.description: express.json() without a limit option — vulnerable to JSON body DoS.

patterns.name: Flask debug=True
patterns.description: Flask debug mode exposes Werkzeug debugger — full RCE via browser.

patterns.name: Django DEBUG = True
patterns.description: Django DEBUG exposes stack traces and settings to users.

patterns.name: Django SECRET_KEY Hardcoded
patterns.description: Django SECRET_KEY as literal — sessions and CSRF tokens can be forged.

patterns.name: assert Used for Auth Check
patterns.description: assert is stripped with python -O — auth checks silently bypassed.

patterns.name: Jinja2 Autoescape Disabled
patterns.description: autoescape=False — template variables unescaped, enabling XSS.

patterns.name: hashlib for Password Hashing
patterns.description: hashlib without PBKDF2/salt is unsuitable for passwords — use bcrypt or argon2.

patterns.name: Python requests with verify=False
patterns.description: TLS verification disabled — all HTTPS requests are MITM-able.

patterns.name: Java Statement SQL Injection

patterns.name: Java Runtime.exec() with User Data
patterns.description: Runtime.exec() with user data — OS command injection.

patterns.name: java.util.Random for Security Context

patterns.name: WebView addJavascriptInterface

patterns.name: Android Component Exported Without Permission

patterns.name: android:debuggable=true
patterns.description: Debuggable APK — ADB shell access on non-rooted devices.

patterns.name: Android usesCleartextTraffic=true
patterns.description: App allows plain HTTP — all traffic is cleartext.

patterns.name: World-Readable File Mode
patterns.description: MODE_WORLD_READABLE — other apps can read this app's files.

patterns.name: Credentials in SharedPreferences
patterns.description: Passwords/tokens in SharedPreferences — plaintext on rooted devices.

patterns.name: Android Log.* with Sensitive Data
patterns.description: Logging passwords/tokens — visible via adb logcat.

patterns.name: TODO: Auth Not Implemented

patterns.name: Auth Check Bypassed in Comment

patterns.name: console.log of Sensitive Data
patterns.description: Logging passwords/tokens — leaks to monitoring and browser devtools.

patterns.name: isDev / isLocal Auth Bypass
patterns.description: Auth gate bypassed when isDev/isLocal — misconfigured env skips all security.

patterns.name: Auth Function Always Returns True
patterns.description: Auth function only returns true — placeholder that was never completed.

patterns.name: Admin by Hardcoded Email Check

patterns.name: Empty catch Block
patterns.description: Empty catch on security operations silently swallows errors — auth bypass by forcing exceptions.

patterns.name: Sensitive Data in URL Query String
patterns.description: Password/token in URL params — logged by servers, proxies, and browsers.

patterns.name: Auth Middleware That Only Calls next()
patterns.description: Middleware calling next() unconditionally — placeholder auth never finished.

patterns.name: Server Bound to 0.0.0.0

patterns.name: Docker --privileged Flag
patterns.description: Running container with --privileged — trivial container escape.

patterns.name: S3 Bucket with Public-Read ACL
patterns.description: S3 ACL public-read — all data publicly accessible.

patterns.name: IAM Policy Wildcard Action (*)
patterns.description: IAM Action:* grants full permissions — follow least privilege.

patterns.name: Hardcoded Public IP Address
patterns.description: Hardcoded non-RFC1918 IP — likely a debug/dev endpoint left in production.

patterns.name: Plaintext HTTP URL to External Host
patterns.description: HTTP to an external host — traffic is unencrypted.

patterns.name: Redis Connection Without Password
patterns.description: Redis client without auth — any client can read all data if port is exposed.

patterns.name: require() from HTTP URL
patterns.description: Loading a module from an HTTP URL — RCE if URL is compromised.

patterns.description: Downloading and executing a remote script — supply chain attack vector.
